summary:
HELIOS is a comprehensive system designed to protect astronauts' physical and mental health during space missions. It integrates artificial intelligence, smartwatches (Open Wearables), and biomedical and environmental sensors to monitor their health, detect risks, and analyze environmental conditions. Additionally, it incorporates the GWM (Gravity & Wellness Module), which uses rotation to generate artificial gravity and counteract some effects of microgravity.

This challenge is addressed through technologies that enable continuous monitoring of astronauts' health and help prevent complications. The system also includes psychological support tools, recommendations for rest, yoga, and physical exercise. It incorporates an Open Wearables smartwatch as an additional monitoring tool. Furthermore, it features two versions of the GWM module: an individual centrifuge (GWM-S) and a rotating habitat (GWM-L). All components are connected to software that analyzes collected data and provides insights to determine solutions to identified problems.

The importance of HELIOS lies in its ability to protect astronauts, reduce risks associated with long-duration space missions, and improve their physical and mental well-being. The project proposes a technological solution that supports safer and more sustainable future space missions.
details:
HELIOS

The project HELIOS (Human Evaluation, Life Indicators & Orbital Surveillance) consists of software designed to continuously monitor and track astronauts’ physical and mental health during space missions. Its main goal is to ensure their safety and well-being by identifying potential health issues, enabling timely decisions and preventing complications.

As part of its functionality, HELIOS includes a digital medical library that provides physical and mental exercises, recommendations, and step-by-step protocols to guide astronauts when changes in their health are detected.

Several tools were used in the development of the project, including Claude, Open Wearables, and Open Anatomy 3D, which supported the research, design, and development of the proposal.

HELIOS stands out as a creative and innovative project because it addresses a real challenge in space exploration: protecting astronauts’ health in environments where access to medical care is limited. Additionally, it proposes the implementation of a physical space inside the spacecraft, designed to help astronauts assess, understand, and improve their physical condition through specific activities and resources.

The expected impact of the project is to help prevent health problems, promote self-care habits, and improve astronauts’ quality of life during their missions, especially on long-duration space journeys.

Regarding artificial intelligence, it was used as a supporting tool to improve the video quality and assist with certain aspects of software development. However, the research, idea generation, design, and most of the development of the proposal were carried out directly by the team members, taking into account factors such as safety, space environmental conditions, resource limitations, and the physical and mental needs of astronauts.
